scope: Affected current math_signature repair and regression tests only; no new N42 content/answer/visual re-review
reasons: Before/current diff is limited to the existing mathcheck.katex_validate import, bounded continuation candidate collection/renderability guard, extra relation guard and focused regression assertions. Tokenization/normalization itself is unchanged.

Each adjacent whitespace-only candidate is identified by raw leading =,+,-; one structured existing KaTeX batch runs only when candidates exist. Inputs retain independent raw TeX and display mode with unique index IDs.

Joining requires BOTH immediately adjacent rows to have ok exactly True. Missing/false results cannot authorize joining. A fatal parser/helper receipt raises SystemExit before signature construction, rather than approving an unchecked concatenation.

The supplied broken fraction cannot now acquire the intact signature: its two independently parsed rows fail renderability, preserving the two-span boundary. The added negative cases also cover unclosed aligned environments, unmatched left/right and missing unbraced fraction arguments.

Complete =-prefixed equation rows can continue, while standalone +/- rows containing =,<,>, or the enumerated le/leq/ge/geq/ne/neq/approx/equiv relation commands are conservatively kept separate. The new a=1 then -b=2 regression explicitly rejects the misleading concatenated equation.

The original TeX token separator, command-token boundaries, braces, all sign/operator tokens and variable/vector names remain unchanged. Existing negative token/group/sign tests remain in the current file; whitespace-only and intended complete N42 additive/equality continuations remain supported.

No concrete new regression in this affected repair was identified. This resolves the original independently-unrenderable-row finding, not a claim that a syntactic fingerprint proves arbitrary mathematical equivalence.
